solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Erase stuff shown by son's notebooks

parts.note: to scratch out or scratch is to delete or cancel
to pad is to stuff or fill out
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone is rubbing things out in their son's exercise books.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratchpads are rough jotters for quick notes, a kind of notebook.

clue.text: 4 disregarding news over tree

indicators.note: disregarding means the letters for news are ignored, left out

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, a high-kicking dance
two Ns, N being the abbreviation for new, so news is N plus N
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue with little surface: ignore the news, think tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as plural N's: two of them come out of CANCAN, leaving CACA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Idiot blonde loses agent's protection

indicators.note: loses means the US agent is dropped from the word for blonde

parts.note: fair-headed means having blonde hair
a Fed is US slang for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A dim blonde is losing a secret agent's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protection' says the agent is the outer layer, split across both ends of the blonde word. 'Idiot blonde' looks like one phrase, but only 'Idiot' defines; blonde is a hyphenated 4-6 adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Airhead is slang for a stupid, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Dance has the power to preserve

parts.note: can means is able, has the power
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: A dance that has the power to keep something going.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is the high-kicking Parisian music-hall dance.

clue.text: All keep moving around university artist

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the university abbreviation
moving means these letters shift to new positions

explanation.surface: Everyone keeps circling the campus, like a restless art student.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter of the Bauhaus era.

clue.text: One who welcomes party with alternative staff

parts.note: a do is a party
or introduces an alternative
to man something is to staff it

explanation.surface: A host greets guests at a party, with stand-by staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman stands at a hotel or club entrance to greet arriving guests.

clue.text: Excellent medicine is way to get out cold

parts.note: a knockout is something stunning or excellent
drops are liquid medicine given a drop at a time

explanation.surface: A wonderful remedy for shaking off a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a cure for a cold; 'out cold' is unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockout drops are a drug slipped into a drink to make someone unconscious.

clue.text: Squeezed company group invested in wine

indicators.note: invested in means put inside the word for wine

parts.note: red is wine
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A firm's consortium puts money into wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A corseted figure is laced tightly into a corset, so squeezed in.

clue.text: Colder city, her cooking supplied by natural power

indicators.note: cooking means these letters are being stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A colder city is warmed by someone's cooking powered by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydroelectric means generated by flowing water, a natural source of power.

clue.text: Better name cool river

parts.note: to ice something is to cool or chill it
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A recommendation that a cooler name be given to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, so it means more pleasant, i.e. better.

clue.text: New term involving ancient city's study of body's impulses

indicators.note: involving means the coined-word term wraps around the old city

parts.note: a neology is a newly coined word or term
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A newly coined phrase describing how an ancient city studied the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New term' looks like N plus a word for term, but it is one piece: NEOLOGY, a coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurology is the branch of medicine dealing with nerves, which carry the body's impulses.

clue.text: Suppress church, certainly with European help

parts.note: OK, an assent, means certainly
to back someone is to support or help them

explanation.surface: A church gets a European helping hand to keep something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke back tears or words is to hold them in, i.e. suppress them.

clue.text: One giving hope, not supporting penny-pincher

indicators.note: not means the word for supporting is to be left out of the hope-giver

parts.note: a promiser is one who makes promises, giving hope
pro means in favour of, supporting

explanation.surface: A hopeful backer who turns out to be stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending it, the very picture of a skinflint.

clue.text: Overcome by drink, is backing daughter's legal position?

indicators.note: overcome by means swallowed up within the word for a drink

parts.note: one as in 'one for the road', a drink

indicators.note: backing means the word is runs backwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A tipsy daughter wonders whether her position is legal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome by drink' suggests drunkenness; here ONE (a drink) surrounds SI (IS reversed by 'backing') and D.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby, a player who is onside is in a legal position; the question mark flags the sporting sense.

clue.text: Mostly grumpy about exam hangover

indicators.note: about means the cut-down grumpy word goes round the exam
mostly means the last letter of the word for grumpy is dropped

parts.note: surly is grumpy
a viva is an oral university exam

explanation.surface: Someone is mostly grumpy about an exam while hungover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangover' is the misleading word: not the morning after, but a relic from earlier times. A VIVA is an oral exam at a British university.
explanation.definitionFit: A survival is a custom or thing that persists from the past, a holdover.

clue.text: Frenchman discovered better light cloth

parts.note: Jean is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: discovered means the cover, the outer letters, is stripped off the next word

explanation.surface: A Frenchman found a better lightweight fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeanette is a light twilled cotton fabric, a lighter relative of jean.

clue.text: Time after moment in heavens is foggiest

indicators.note: after means the time abbreviation comes last
in means the word for a moment is placed inside the heavens

parts.note: the skies are the heavens
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A weather report: shortly, the skies will be at their foggiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokiest means thickest with smoke or haze, close to foggiest.

clue.text: Anger in the majority being overturned: electorate's conclusion is 'boring'

indicators.note: in means the word for anger is placed inside
being overturned means the word for majority is turned upside down in this across answer, i.e. read backwards

parts.note: most means the majority
ire is anger

indicators.note: conclusion means the final letter of electorate's

explanation.surface: A political lament: angry voters overturn the majority, and the result is tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome wearies you, which is what boring means.

clue.text: Woman from South America meeting Henry's second wife

parts.note: US is America
Anne Boleyn was Henry VIII's second wife

explanation.surface: A woman from South America meets Henry VIII's second queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' is not the continent; it splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Susanne is a female first name, so a woman.

clue.text: Stop working after idiot mostly becomes eating obsessive

indicators.note: after means the word for stop working follows the shortened idiot
mostly means the last letter of the word for idiot is dropped

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: An idiot stops working and becomes obsessed with eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A foodie is an enthusiast for fine cuisine, someone obsessed with eating well.

clue.text: Displeasure from Church consuming Slough

indicators.note: consuming means the preposition and church eat up the word for slough

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
CE is the Church of England
a fen is a marsh, as is a slough

explanation.surface: The Church is displeased that Slough is being swallowed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town near London, but here it is a bog, as in Bunyan's 'Slough of Despond'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence is to feel displeasure or resentment.

clue.text: Article supporting cut with raised cover

indicators.note: supporting means, in a down answer, the article sits underneath
raised means the letter for with moves up, towards the top of this down answer

parts.note: to saw is to cut
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An article backs up a cut that has had a cover lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' lifts the W in SAW higher in the down light, giving SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or bandage, so to cover.

clue.text: Acts like a Viking god, one sad on reflection when Freya finally leaves

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: leaves means the final letter of the goddess's name goes out of the reversed word
on reflection means the word sad is mirrored, read backwards
finally means the last letter of Freya

explanation.surface: Norse mythology: a god behaves like a Viking, a sad figure once Freya departs.
explanation.walkthrough: SAD read backwards is DAS; 'leaves' takes away A, Freya's last letter, giving DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were famous for sudden attacks on coasts, so to act like one is to make raids.

clue.text: Hairy grub's wife provided most of destruction within equipment

indicators.note: within means these pieces go inside the word for equipment

parts.note: kit is equipment
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is lost

parts.note: ruin is destruction

explanation.surface: A furry caterpillar's wife wrecked most of the kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like a larva, the hairy caterpillar of the surface, but it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal for food, and the kiwi fruit has a fuzzy brown skin, so it is hairy food.

clue.text: Forbidden to rear duck inside — it's designed to dive

indicators.note: inside means the zero-score letter goes within
to rear means lifted up, reading backwards in a down answer

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape O

explanation.surface: It's forbidden to raise a duck inside; it's built to dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, built to go underwater.

clue.text: I will enter factory with former partner first to translate unencoded writing

indicators.note: will enter means the letter I goes into the word for a factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory
an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of translate

explanation.surface: Instructions for a code-breaker: get into the factory with an ex, then translate.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain text is a message before encryption or after decryption, readable without a cipher.

clue.text: Ancient mother-in-law I grumble about

indicators.note: about means the pronoun and the word for grumble are turned round together

parts.note: to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: Someone admits to complaining about their mother-in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is the mother-in-law Ruth follows, saying 'whither thou goest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi, in the Old Testament, is Ruth's mother-in-law, from biblical times.

clue.text: The French badly treat the English imitation hide

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: badly means these letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The French mistreat the English, a fake-leather insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherette is a synthetic material made to look like animal skin, i.e. fake leather.
